Armored Battleboars are ferocious boars found in the Battleboar Pen on Red Cloud Mesa. Chief Squealer Thornmantle is a quilboar and the leader of the Bristleback tribe. He was originally known simply as "Squealer" Thornmantle and could be found in Brambleblade Ravine.

After the death of Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle, Squealer took leadership of the tribe and became known as Chief Squealer Thornmantle. He led the Bristleback attack on Camp Narache, killing Greatmother Hawkwind. He fled and hid afterwards and now hides in Thornmantle's Hideout, fending off any braves the tauren send in after him. Adana Thunderhorn asks adventurers to kill Thornmantle and bring his mane back to Chief Hawkwind in honor of the Greatmother.

Gazelles are small, hooved gazelles native to the Barrens as well as Desolace and Mulgore. They often travel in herds.

Some Sickly Gazelles have become poisoned by the corrupted waters of Dreadmist Peak and require the aid of a healing salve to restore them to normal.
sections.To All The Squirrels I've Loved Before:
Those seeking to complete To All The Squirrels I've Loved Before may have more luck finding a herd in the Southern Barrens (in the broad vicinity of Camp Taurajo) or to the north and west of Forgotten Pools in the Northern Barrens - however gazelles can be found running anywhere in the zone. Herds of gazelles move fairly quickly.

Note that Sickly Gazelles do not count towards the To All The Squirrels I've Loved Before achievement.

sections.Description: Ghost Howl is a wolf found roaming the plains around the base of Thunder Bluff in Mulgore.
sections.Background:
Ghost Howl is a massive white wolf and a respected beast among the tauren for his aid against the Burning Legion. During the Ghost Howl's battles he attained a savage wound from a particularly nasty demon. Despite Azeroth's victory, the wolf continues to carry the wound, the pain of an unhealable wound tormenting his spirit and causing him to grow hostile towards the tauren and their allies. He now spends his final days roaming Mulgore in solitude.

The aging hunter Skorn Whitecloud, resident of Bloodhoof Village, once encountered the mighty Ghost Howl in his youth and, though unsuccessful in his own attempts to end the wolf's suffering spirit, commends those adventurers able to slay and salvage his demon-scarred hide.
sections.Strategies: The key to finding Ghost Howl is mainly patience. He is an uncommon mob and won't always be where common sightings say he is. He has been spotted the most times around , the ditch just off to the West of the main road before heading up into Thunder Bluff. His roaming path also seems to span up and around the very North-West/North-East parts of the region, all within relative distance to Thunder Bluff.
sections.Notes:
- In order to get the quest for killing Ghost Howl, you must kill him first and then right-click on the Demon Scarred Cloak to be prompted by the Quest text. You can also wear the item after you've handed it in by dragging it onto your Back item slot. Right-clicking does not work.
- After you've completed the quest for Ghost Howl, Skorn Whitecloud will now always say, "You killed Ghost Howl. You're a stud.", when spoken to.
- Ghost Howl is tameable.
sections.Speculation: Though his exact contributions are vague, Skorn doesn't mention whether they fought during the War of the Ancients or the Third War it can be assumed that Ghost Howl fought against the Burning Legion's army in an attempt to take Mulgore during the Legion's second invasion and the Battle of Mount Hyjal.

sections.Description:
Orno Grimtotem is a Magatha loyalist and the leader of the Grimtotem forces invading Mulgore. His Grimtotem forces corrupted the water wells within the region while he made his pass of operations at Stonetalon Pass. However, Baine's forces were able to heal the wells and find out his location. As his Grimtotem Defenders were engaged with Thunder Bluff Braves, Orno was noted to be observing the battlefield before being confronted by an agent of the Horde.

During the subsequent battle, Orno became enraged when he realized there was a chance that he could lose. Upon this realization, he stunned his opponent and then was subsequently confronted by Baine Bloodhoof. Seeing this is to be the perfect chance, Orno ignored his former foe and ordered his men to attack the young Bloodhoof. However, Baine would prove himself to be no weakling and Orno would lose his life.

sections.Description: Supervisor Fizsprocket is a goblin member of the Venture Company and the supervisor of the Venture Co. Mine in Mulgore. The Venture Co. was refused mining rights in Mulgore, but they would not take no for an answer. Mogul Razdunk and the company's advisory board were encouraging Fizsprocket to expand Mulgore operations to lumber harvesting as well. The board was going to provide the supervisor with several of their newest model shredders and raw materials to construct a mill. The tauren in the area were enraged with his mining division in their delicate land. Tauren Outrunners had destroyed one of the supply caravans on its way to the mine, and Morin Cloudstalker asked adventurers to kill Fizsprocket and take his clipboard.

sections.History: The Rake was formerly one of the most commonly seen hunter pets due to his attack speed of 1.2, the second-best attack speed available in a tameable pet. The only ones faster were Broken Tooth and the Bloodseeker Bat with a 1.0 attack speed, though there are a few other beasts that also had a 1.2 attack speed. Since pet attack-speed normalization in patch 2.0.1, he has lost this significance. Numerous savannah cats in the Barrens are identical in appearance, and are easily available for taming. Since Deathwing's return, the Rake's only attack is Leaping Rush.

sections.Description: The Bountiful Tables are tables set up during the Pilgrim's Bounty world event. Several tables are located outside the main cities (Orgrimmar, Thunder Bluff, Undercity, and Silvermoon City for Horde; Stormwind City, Ironforge, Darnassus, and The Exodar for Alliance), and smaller groups of tables can be found at various other towns.
sections.How the table works:
Each Bountiful Table has 5 chairs around it, allowing up to 5 characters to sit at one table. Each seat is named for the Pilgrim's Bounty dish shown to the right of that location:
- The Turkey Chair ( Slow-Roasted Turkey )
- The Cranberry Chair ( Cranberry Chutney )
- The Stuffing Chair ( Spice Bread Stuffing )
- The Sweet Potato Chair ( Candied Sweet Potato )
- The Pie Chair ( Pumpkin Pie )

The chairs use the vehicle mechanics in that you "mount" it, and while there are provided an action bar unique to that position. 

Each seat at the table is in easy reach of one dish. Initially, only two options are available: pass your dish, and "eat (your dish)".

The first option of each chair is "pass your dish", with the dish icon representing the dish you can reach on the table. Target one of the other chairs, and select this option, to pass your dish to that chair. If someone is sitting in that chair, AND already has that dish on their plate, you bounce the food off their head. (In the case of the chutney, 'theoretically', since chutney is not well known for bouncing...). Otherwise, it adds your dish to that plate, even if nobody is currently sitting there. 

The other 5 options presented are to eat the food depicted (turkey, chutney, stuffing, sweet potato, or pie). As others pass their dish (to you), those options will become enabled.

Eating any of the food at the table gives you a short-lived (5 minute) buff, with the buff icon showing that food item. These buffs stack up to 5. If you get all 5 buffs up to 5, you lose those buffs and gain instead The Spirit of Sharing, a 60 minute buff that increases your reputation gains by 10%.
sections.Related achievements:
- - bounce food off a given person's head
- - acquire The Spirit of Sharing at all four of your faction's capital cities.
- - pass one of each dish
- - take a seat at a bountiful table at each enemy capital.
sections.Objective of: - Celebration of Sharing
sections.Notes:
"Bouncing food off another person's head" is done by passing food while you have someone targeted and they already have a full stack of that food available. You can get the warning "invalid target" if you try passing food while having someone targeted who is not at the table.

Food from other positions at the table are consumed, and may need to be passed again. You can also move to another chair.

Food passed from another chair will last for up to 5 minutes at that position unless consumed first.

__NOTOC__

Prairie Dogs are a type of ground squirrel found on grassy plains throughout Azeroth (especially on Kalimdor), as well as in both versions of Nagrand.
sections.Pet Journal: Distinct from their tree dwelling cousins, these ground squirrels make their homes on the plains of Azeroth and beyond.
sections.Notes:

- Prairie Dogs, Rabbits and Mice can be seen occasionally donning helmets and rifles on a plateau high above Stonetalon Pass, Mulgore.
- In , Prairie Dog Musk allows hunters to tame Prairie Dogs as companion pets.
